Hi Marissa —

Thanks — that plan sounds good. A few clarifications so we can prep:

1) Auth: Our infra team prefers short-lived credentials backed by our IdP (Okta) and key wrapping in KMS. Can Redwood support ephemeral tokens obtained via a token exchange (OIDC client) instead of long-lived API keys for the POC?

2) Routing: We need deterministic routing rules we can control from our service — e.g., route by model tag (low-cost-embed, high-quality-chat) and fallback to a cheaper variant if latency > 500ms. Is that configurable via SDK or do we need separate endpoints?

3) Structured output: We saw tool-calling in the demo. If streaming is enabled, what is the recommended pattern to ensure the JSON schema isn’t broken mid-stream? Will Redwood provide incremental parse hints or do we need to buffer until end-of-stream?

4) Tokenization/max_tokens: For chat-style histories, how does Redwood count tokens vs our internal tokenizer? We have hard limits and need predictable billing/limits per request. Also, how do 'stop' sequences interact with streaming — can a stop trigger an early close of the stream and still return valid structured JSON?

If you can get Ethan / Dev on a call Thu 9am PT, that works for us.

Best,

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up + technical questions (SDK, auth, RSP schema)

Jordan / Priya —

Quick answers before the call, and we’ll deep-dive on Thu:

Auth
- We support both API keys (long-lived) and ephemeral tokens via token-exchange (OIDC). For POCs we typically show a flow where Acme’s backend exchanges an Okta-issued id_token for a Redwood short-lived token (1 hour TTL). That token can be automatically rotated by the SDK or obtained via our token endpoint.
- KMS/HSM: we don’t store customer keys in plaintext. We support envelope encryption integrations with AWS KMS / Google KMS and can sign/verify requests via customer-managed keys for Private deployments.

Routing
- Routing policies are configurable in our control plane and exposed via SDK config. You can define route rules by model tag, latency thresholds, and cost tiers. Example rule: if latency > 500ms AND model == high-quality-chat -> route to chat-fallback-1.
- SDK includes a 'RouteSuggestion' API that returns a signed routing decision; engineers can call it before sending the request or use agent-based automatic routing.

Structured output & streaming
- Tool-calling/structured JSON: when streaming is enabled we stream tokens as produced. To avoid broken JSON you have two options: 1) buffer until stream completes and then parse (recommended for strict JSON), or 2) use our 'chunked-json' framing where each semantic chunk is emitted as a complete JSON object with a trailing delimiter.
- We also emit incremental parse hints in the stream metadata (e.g., partial_object_start, partial_object_end) so client can safely apply incremental parsers. The SDK provides parsers for both patterns (buffered and streaming-parse).

Tokenization / max_tokens / stop behavior
- Tokenization: Redwood uses the model's native tokenizer for token accounting (we surface token counts in the response metadata). For pre-tokenized inputs you can also supply token counts to our API to skip server-side tokenization.
- max_tokens: this is a per-request cap on generated tokens. For chat we count tokens across role/name/system messages + prompt; generated tokens are counted against max_tokens.
- stop sequences: we support both string-based stops and token-based stops. When a stop is triggered mid-stream, we send a stream event 'stopped' and close the stream — if using chunked-json framing the last chunk will be a complete JSON object. If you rely on plain streaming into an open JSON object, you should use the SDK's streaming parser to handle premature termination gracefully.

Billing predictability
- We provide a preflight token estimation endpoint: send your request (no billing) and get an estimated token usage + probability mass for stop sequences. Use it to enforce client-side limits.

Call prep
- For Thu 09:00 PT we’ll bring a short demo showing: ephemeral token flow (Okta -> Redwood), route rules example, and streaming chunked-json parser for tool-calling. I’ll also bring a sample script for embeddings -> reranker.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Staff Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com
